classification.difficultyReason: Read zeroes and strict positive and negative intervals from supplied quadratic graphs, including an unlabelled origin crossing.

content.prompt: For each parabola, state the values of $x$ for which:

spec.description: Unfilled upward parabola with roots 1 and 3, y-intercept 3, positive axis arrows and arrows at both curve ends. No grid.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph and numerical labels remain visible; answers are separate.

answer.worked: The curve meets the $x$-axis at $x=1$ and $x=3$, so these are the values for which $y=0$.
The curve is above the $x$-axis outside its two intercepts. Hence $x<1$ or $x>3$.
The curve is below the $x$-axis between its intercepts. Hence $1<x<3$.

spec.description: Unfilled upward parabola with roots −4 and 2, y-intercept −8, positive axis arrows and arrows at both curve ends. No grid.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph only; no solution intervals are marked.

answer.worked: The curve meets the $x$-axis at $x=-4$ and $x=2$, where $y=0$.
The curve lies above the $x$-axis outside its intercepts. Hence $x<-4$ or $x>2$.
The curve lies below the $x$-axis between its intercepts. Hence $-4<x<2$.

spec.description: Unfilled downward parabola crossing the unlabelled origin and x=5, positive axis arrows and arrows at both curve ends. No zero label or grid.
spec.mathematics: y=x(5-x); only the zeroes and concavity are assessed.
spec.answerVisibility: Origin crossing is a permanent given but is not labelled with its answer value.

answer.worked: The curve meets the $x$-axis at the origin and at $x=5$. Hence $y=0$ when $x=0$ or $x=5$.
The curve lies above the $x$-axis between its intercepts. Hence $0<x<5$.
The curve lies below the $x$-axis outside its intercepts. Hence $x<0$ or $x>5$.
